reviews.text: The genre of the film is supposed to be a new take on film noir and detectives, but if Nick is supposed to be a type of detective that has seen it all, how does he get fooled into believing that his hottest client was just looking for her keys
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: It is a true delight to see how Ferguson and Newton escape the limitations that usually accompany female archetypes in this genre. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Reminiscence's official synopsis is gripping with an air of mystery around it. To the misfortune of the film itself, the film in its entirety is deeply impaired by its unexciting, deficient take...
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: Reminiscence is full of potential but fails to live up to it. It aims for the heights of hard boiled film noir classic but sadly the result is nearer soft boiled. For a film all about the power of memory, the end result is ironically entirely forgettable.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: While Jackman and Ferguson are excellent here, Reminiscence is a watered-down sci-fi neo-noir that overstays its welcome by wallowing in a romance that loses steam fast.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Despite its promise, “Reminiscence” is more of a sampler platter of numerous better films.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Its really telling when offhand details about the societal collapse and war that led to this water-damaged future are far more fascinating than the actual plot, but it leads to Reminiscence feeling like a bad episode of an otherwise solid TV show.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: The film is bland and boring with a plot that makes no sense and emotion that fails to hit.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: The reality is that watching Reminiscence is an endurance test. It's two hours of Jackman's character, the sour-faced Nick Bannister, scowling through scenes and unloading exposition in his omnipresent voiceover.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Reminiscence is full of desperate people saying maudlin things, packing in as much exposition as mechanically as they can.
reviews.author: Zosha Millman

reviews.text: The war and the vast gorge between the haves and have-nots exists merely as a blurry backdrop for Nick's vague, navel-gazey crapola about the nature of loss and memory and the melancholy passage of time.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Where the film and director Joy get a little tangled up is when an attempt is made to stuff too much into the story all at once.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: A swampy mystery, a soggy action film, and a waterlogged love story.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The acting talent can carry this movie only so far but eventually, the disjointed and clichéd script falls apart so much that nothing can save it.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: There're layers upon layers in Reminiscence which imply incredible thought and planning on Joy's part, most of which come together in a solid and satisfying way.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Although it has an undeniable appeal in conceptual terms, it's burden by a dull and nonrhythmic narrative, and by a string of -very- common and pompous places.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: The right beginning and end are present, the journey is just too convoluted and overstuffed to gracefully connect them.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Many films we now consider "classics" were initially met with disdain, indifference and befuddlement and Reminiscence fits that mold. This is a title which begs to be viewed not twice, but multiple times and I can't wait to watch it repeatedly.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: Despite its technical feats, this noir thriller is so bleak and dense you don't want to keep it in your memories. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: The detours can be frustrating, but the branches are often interesting to venture across, as is the experience of watching a major motion picture willing to reach as far down a rabbit hole as "Reminiscence" does.
reviews.author: Luke Parker

reviews.text: Reminiscence features several people submerged in a water tank as they recover or relive their memories. Ironically, this ill-conceived movie is utterly forgettable, as it submerges viewers in a story that's both convoluted and predictable.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Reminiscence feels like a glitchy plot generator set to All. Mobsters, drug deals, lounge singers, illegitimate children, unfinished love affairs, tossed in and set to puree
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: Joy knows how to build mesmerizing dark places filled with broken people looking for hope, love, and redemption; now she just needs to refine and polish that vision.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: Beyond the surface novelty of the setting and premise, there's not much here that could exactly be called original. But the layering of reflections and shadows has a ghostly glamour of its own.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: This movie can plod at times due to its flashback-driven structure. However, the unusual setting and the ever-reliable Jackman keeps things moving when absolutely necessary.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Reminiscence tips its hat respectfully to many of its predecessors, but behind that, it struggles to stand out on its own. Reminiscence still shows promise for whatever Lisa Joy decides to do next...
reviews.author: Andrew Dex

reviews.text: What we're left with is a bit of a mess, but one that tackles big ideas and is not afraid to be corny. To call it good would be a stretch, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't leave the theater fairly satisfied.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: A movie about revelling in the past that happily plays it safe instead of striding into the future.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Visually compelling and front-loaded with an attractive cast, the science-fiction film Reminiscence has the added bonus of being a deeply layered film with noir story and dialogue.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Reminiscence's waterlogged world provides a potentially interesting backdrop, but it never really comes to life as a key ingredient.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Shoves myriad genres into a too-bloated film that flounders and goes nowhere.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Characters talk to each other with words that feel like sermons and the plot goes nowhere before finally tapping out.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: Reminiscence is, ironically, a very forgettable film.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Overly reliant on tropes that have been done to death, Reminiscence emerges as an inert ghost of the past with no innate value or meaning.
reviews.author: Debopriyaa Dutta

reviews.text: While the film has the right feel, it lacks soul and true intent.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Reminiscence may be flawed, but it is a deeply haunting portrait of a man too weak for this world.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: The visuals are artistically fantastic, and the score strong, unfortunately the script/dialogue, impact, and pacing lack.
reviews.author: Ross Anthony

reviews.text: The feeling of groundedness is reinforced by the reliance on grand yet practical water-based sets and effects.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Like its characters, it's drunk on what came before, relying too heavily on noir tropes. But its smart, thought-provoking concept isn't so easy to shake off.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: A lot of talent is squandered in this could have been so much better film. Still it holds your attention with its murky story and glorious sets.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Lisa Joy developed a very interesting basic idea for her directorial debut... ,[but] Joy makes it difficult for the public to empathize with the characters, you can tell that she's being rushed by her own story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The cast deserved better, the audience certainly deserves better, and maybe we should just take the film's own advice and forget we ever saw it.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: ...sci-fi should be a fun way of exploring new ideas, but unfortunately the over-stuffed version featuring in Lisa Joy's version is far too derivative of previous models...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: There's too much going on in Reminiscence when it needs subtlety and a specific focus. Lisa Joy has a grab bag of ideas and genres at play hoping enough stick to make this all come together in the end.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Gorgeous visuals with an intriguing concept. Its runtime works a bit against it, but the third act saves the film.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: The film indeed has an extent of creativity and smart twists that the audience will be able to enjoy .. if they can make it past the first half
reviews.author: Mahmoud Mahdy

reviews.text: If Reminiscence makes the viewer nostalgic for anything-besides Blade Runner and Nolan's filmography-it'd be for a time when original tentpoles weren't rare enough that their very existence needs to be commended.
reviews.author: Miles Surrey

reviews.text: As the logical gaps widen beyond repair, and the melodramatic coincidences yield more questions than answers, you'll want to forget you watched it.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: For a movie about memory and its powerful hold on us, Reminiscence never finds a way to lodge itself in one's mind.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: While it's a gorgeous picture, the plot is ridiculous, especially once it hits the third act.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Its intriguing premise is hampered by tired tropes, forehead-slapping dialogue, and ham-fisted narration.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: While it has a nifty look and a potentially intriguing premise, it ends up squandering both on a tired and convoluted narrative that borrows ideas from any number of properties.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: A hodgepodge of genres and tones, Reminiscence commits the cardinal sin of being so uninteresting that it basically invites the viewer to fondly recall the older movies that it brazenly rips off.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Perhaps the filmmaker is trying to go for slo-burn suspense, evoking the tone and vibe of celebrated classic noir. But it's not a good sign when the intended slow build tension ends up becoming dreary and tedious.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: It's not the smoothest ride getting to the end of this convoluted plot, but I though [the cast] was great.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: In the end I felt as numbed and bummed as Jackman's character, but for all the wrong reasons.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Reminiscence is a good example of how wonderfully pleasing the genre can be even when it's not really doing too much aside from slapping a fresh coat of paint on old-school pulp stories.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Blandly stylish and sporadically intriguing.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Writer/director Lisa Joy creates a mesmerizing blend of ambition and craft.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: The multilayered memory playbacks owe a debt to the dream worlds of Christopher Nolan's Inception, although this is ultimately a much more accessible movie.
reviews.author: Terry Staunton

reviews.text: [I]f Joy somehow gets to make another feature after such a disastrous debut, hopefully, someone else will do the writing.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: [Reminiscence] leaves you remembering other, better films and wondering about what might have been - oddly ironic for a story where the toxicity of nostalgia is a central tenet...This film steeped in memory ultimately proves sadly forgettable.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Reminiscence could have been a fresh way to provide commentary on current world issues with riveting storytelling. What you get instead is a forced plot that is neither compelling or worth its nearly two-hour run time.
reviews.author: Chauncey K. Robinson

reviews.text: Joy doesn't lack for ideas. It's just that there are too many and few of them original.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Alas, the real reminiscence is of previous and better movies of this sort.
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: If hyper-serious, hyper-stylized pastiche is your jam, Reminiscence might be for you. The rest of us may find ourselves forgetting it in short order.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: The corny script and the static direction are both by Lisa Joy from the TV show Westworld. This is her first feature film. It probably won't be her last, but hope springs eternal.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Reminiscence will fade into memory and won't be one I'll look to revisit.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Jackman puts his brooding charisma to good use, giving Nick the dark shading a noir antihero needs.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: While the story... is full of good ideas and features a femme fatale as monumental as Rebecca Ferguson, its (unconscious?) efforts to sabotage itself end up weighing too heavily. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yago García

reviews.text: Reminiscence is an assured big-screen debut from Lisa Joy, playfully recreating classic movie tropes with a modern twist.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: Long and trying film.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: It's as if the film itself is [wearing a costume] - and there's not much beneath that layer.
reviews.author: Allison Shoemaker

reviews.text: As a director [Lisa Joy] has a great handle on the film's two major edge-of-your-seat action set pieces. She also gets stellar performances from her cast.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: It's a clever tale, anchored by Jackman doing reliable work as an antihero haunted by his sins.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: As a noir mystery, Reminiscence is certainly solid, with a series of complications and surprising reveals.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: Sadly, nothing ever really gels, making Reminiscence more a collection of ideas in search of cohesion than a good movie.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: Reminiscence has imagination to spare, but it doesn't deliver the precious memories it promises.
reviews.author: Anna Smith

reviews.text: Lots of great ideas & casting but nothing gels as it should.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Captivating as it depicts well-delineated, three-dimensional characters. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Roberto Landaverde

reviews.text: It's difficult to make movie magic with a clunky, cliche-filled, confusing script and plodding, melodramatic pacing.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: An original, neo-noir story with a cool cinematography, weaving in elements of sci-fi, mystery, thriller, crime drama and romance. While far from a mind-blowing trip, the concept, central mystery and cinematography are still worth a trip.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: A sad debut feature for Lisa Joy, the co-creator, often executive producer and producer, and sometimes writer of HBO's highly regarded Westworld series. Her vision here totters between genres and usually just reminds you of better film....
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: Lisa Joy has the potential to be a major film-maker.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: We are definitely on familiar, well-travelled ground, which explains why the visually impressive Reminiscence is good but falls well short of great.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The director has great fun playing with genre tropes, but it's unclear whether she's going for heightened camp.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Joy's script has too much faith in the poignancy of melancholy yearning. The action scenes and the details of the film's invented world are a slightly better source of fun.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: It's just a shame that the score and the cinematography were much stronger than the plot on this occasion.
reviews.author: Lucy Buglass

reviews.text: The stuffy, ominous visual atmosphere is the biggest part of what makes Reminiscence come together.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: There's decent banter between Thandiwe Newton (my pick of the cast) and Hugh Jackman but Reminiscence doesn't make the most of its great ideas.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Joy takes another turn at perception bending with a cocktail of film noir, cli-fi (climate fiction), and action-thriller that is instantly recognizable for fans of those genres
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Adopting a futuristic setting and applying a noir mentality to its narrative, Westworld co-creator Lisa Joy shows bold, original footing in her debut as a feature filmmaker.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Missing the poetry of film noir, this dystopian tale borrows parts of better movies and reassembles them into an unmemorable package.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: Rife with visuals that evoke a disquieting dreamlike state, the story, an ersatz neo-noir set mostly between sunset and sunrise, drones along with the cinematic equivalent of a mosquito's interminable buzz on a humid afternoon.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Reminiscence marks an ambitious if unwieldy directorial debut from Lisa Joy anchored by a high concept story and solid performance from Hugh Jackman.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: With Reminiscence, I am thankful for the return of a good noir, and adding the sci-fi angle makes it that much better.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: You almost need a flow chart to keep track of all the intersecting subplots and even then, it's still a dream one would rather forget.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: ...an intriguing premise that is, for the most part, employed to hopelessly underwhelming and uninvolving effect...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: What separates Reminiscence (2021) from the myriad of dream/memory-based films made during the previous decade involves the exquisite dialogue ...
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: I can't help but cheer on a high concept, original film that knows exactly what it is.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Skip the echoes it offers and go to the originals. If you're going to take a trip down memory lane anyway, better just to cut right to the good stuff.
reviews.author: Tim Stevens

reviews.text: There are so many plot reversals that eventually you stop caring.
reviews.author: Andy Klein

reviews.text: It wants to be Chinatown meets Blade Runner, but it has about the worst dialogue I've heard in a film in forever.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: After a strong start, the plot begins going in multiple directions, never settling on any specific tone. At times, I just wanted to yell at the screen, telling the film to pick a lane and stay in it.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Reminiscence is a throwback sci-fi noir that adds a compelling romance to keep viewers engaged. The mystery will keep you on your toes until the very end.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: A sad combination of Inception and Blade Runner, but it lacks the finer parts that made both of those movies good.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Reminiscence had a thought-provoking story it could have explored in its back pocket, but it instead chose the dull route while keeping the climate change one merely as a backdrop.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: For a film about memory, Reminiscence might just leave you struggling to find much worth remembering.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: A cautionary tale about getting mired in the past is itself hamstrung by what has come before: overplayed noir tropes and underbaked sci-fi ideas. The fab cast at least elevates this to the mediocre.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Reminiscence is a grandiose sci-fi blockbuster that looks great, sounds deafening, but ultimately disappoints because it's a genre-sampler that can't find a distinctive voice of its own.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: Once Reminiscence gets rolling, it's a slick and satisfying ride that barrels to an ending that is suitably beautiful and bleak.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Although initially intriguing and always beautiful to look at (Westworld production designer Howard Cummings and his team are the real stars here), Reminiscence just doesn't have the goods in terms of tension or pace.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: The film aims high, and while it does not really hit that mark, it does deliver good entertainment for those up for its classic noir/sci-fi mash-up.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: All in all, Reminiscence is a promising idea poorly executed.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Joy's film has the courage of its narrative and aesthetic convictions, but not its emotions.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: Requires unearned patience from viewers as the whole thing gradually reaches its ultimate resolution, and even that's underwhelming, joining the rest of this dreary and laborious film.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: This genre entry is disappointingly middling and ironically, unmemorable.
reviews.author: Jeanmarie Tan

reviews.text: Futuristic film noir Reminiscence from Westworld executive producer fails to come together. Jackman and Ferguson have no chemistry. Some memories better left forgotten.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: The plot and the production design are largely forgettable but Joy poses some intriguing questions about memory and the role we cast for ourselves in the stories of our lives.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Reminiscence is the damnedest thing - a movie filled with promising concepts it doesn't get around to exploring, because it's dedicated to a romantic mystery that's never very romantic or mysterious.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: What hurts the movie the most is you can see all the wasted potential. A good idea, a solid director, and a talented cast...that never kicks into second gear.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: A ponderous piece of retro storytelling gussied up with futuristic flourishes.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Perhaps the greatest crime of Reminiscence is how effortlessly it wastes the collective appeal of its A-list cast.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Reminiscence is never even remotely boring, and its relative slickness and earnestness go down quite smoothly, even as you can't help but eye-roll at the sheer silliness of it all.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: There isn't enough here that will linger on the mind for very long.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: If certainly heavy-handed in its political allusions, one still gets the feeling its creatives ultimately just wanted to do their little '90s throwback hard-boiled sci-fi noir.
reviews.author: Ethan Vestby

reviews.text: Even Hugh Jackman's indisputable star power can't light up the pretentious, pseudo-poetic, sci-fi murk of this thundering misfire, which will only make you remember other, better movie mindbenders. 'Blade Runner' anyone?
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: For a film about memories, Reminiscence is ultimately truly forgettable.
reviews.author: Sarah Hagi

reviews.text: A burdensome slog.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Although Reminiscence is made with care and competence and features a strong underlying premise, the film as a whole is forgettable.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: "Reminiscence" is an unintelligible mess.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Blade Runner meets Chinatown meets...a J Crew catalog? Hugh Jackman is a great actor but unfortunately miscast here. Unfortunate misfire from Lisa Joy.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: It's more than a bit disappointing to watch as Joy's initial world-building and establishment of tone become diminished...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Hugh Jackman and Rebecca Ferguson sizzle, and the film's at its best when it focuses on their relationship.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: What we have here is a science-fiction-time-travel private-eye-investigation-procedural-film-noir-love-story.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Action, romance, and corruption mix together in a blend that allows Reminiscence to wow as an original movie that indulges in the comforts of a very familiar sort of story.
reviews.author: Mike Reyes

reviews.text: Derivativeness is not the problem -- all these stories stem from somewhere -- but the lack of imagination, coupled with the film's deadly earnest tone, is another matter entirely.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: An impressive debut for Lisa Joy, who delivers vision, warmth & incredible world-building. A romantic neo-noir film, parts Inception, Blade Runner 2049 and LA Confidential. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: An incomprehensible mess, & waste of time. Sci-fi that needs much more editing-of-purpose and clarity in the fog of its weird story. Rebecca Ferguson seems lost, for example.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Reminiscence's noir adornments inadvertently feel closer to parody than loving homage.
reviews.author: Wes Greene

reviews.text: I sank into restlessness and thought of a phrase from "Krapp's Last Tape," not a movie but the peerless play by Samuel Beckett -- "drowned in dreams and burning to be gone." While Nick was doing the drowning, I was doing the burning.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Joy strains to create a Bladerunner vibe, but a generic quality and the lead characters to go with it prove too much to overcome.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Jackson's emotional performance anchors the movie even if the narrative sometimes drifts away.
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: It's visually inviting, but as flimsy as a paper doll in its themes.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Reminiscence captures that nostalgic energy of old school storytelling in such a loving and passionate manner while making it her own with a compelling sci-fi twist.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: The way Jackman rattles around this effects-laden landscape, looking dissatisfied and lost, serves as a reminder of how gratifyingly uninterested Jackman has seemed in franchise-building in recent years.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: You almost wish Reminiscence were a TV series so you could spend more time in this world and exploring different facets of memory. The flooded future looks like what Venice must have been like in Blade Runner.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: In the end, "Reminiscence's" meta-narrative isn't simply a valentine for movie buffs or fans of film noir, but a cutting edge, haunting examination of obsessive love, the sort best enjoyed in the dark.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Although Reminiscence doesn't try to hide any inherent metaphors, it doesn't do much with the material besides fashion something like a a dull-edged Blade Runner.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Reminiscence moves at a snail's pace. Huge chunks of the film is like watching molasses drip backwards in slow motion.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Reminiscence is all flash and no substance, doing little to earn the emotional catharsis it so desperately wants.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: In "Reminiscence," the past is always a little too present.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Too many of the points the story earns for ambition get deducted for execution in this jumble of ideas.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: It makes no sense (despite all the explaining), but it draws you in with genre beats, pretty people and the professional polish of its machined parts.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Disappointingly derivative...
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Another puzzle box mystery whose intelligence is simultaneously broadcast by and limited by its criss-crossing flashbacks and speeches, none of which are as smart as they are busy.
reviews.author: Simon Abrams

reviews.text: Luckily there's Jackman, Ferguson and Newton, plus Cliff Curtis... whose performances bring this film noir to fruition. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Strictly a welding job, grabbing parts of "Blade Runner," a bolt and a nut or two from "Vertigo" and notions of commercially desired fantasies of pasts real and imagined, straight from "Westworld."
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: For a project with the potential to combine the likes of Inception and Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, Reminiscence instead offers joyless forgettable nonsense.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Reminiscence is a rather generic high concept science fiction story is elevated by some fascinating worldbuilding that would have benefited from more time to explore it.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: You can't help feeling that you've seen this movie before.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Enjoyably dense but a little plodding.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: The whole thing tips overboard, sunk by the weight of its own silliness.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: This genre and mind-bending film tries to do way too much with its various elements but manages to remain mysteriously intriguing and memorable
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: With the star power here and the dystopian setting Reminiscence should have been a sure fire home run, but I had my worries. The villains are one-dimensional. The story runs like a bad detective piece, with cheap romance and melodrama laced throughout.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: Reminiscence may not be unforgettable, but it'll linger in the brain longer than most.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: I admire the ambition but it felt very repetitive and didn't have the emotional umph for it to work
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: While there are flourishes of genuine brilliance, 'Reminiscence' ironically leaves you fondly remembering those films that did this style of cinema more effectively.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: It won't be immediately forgotten, but rather forever known as that time WB gave the co-creator of Westworld a bunch of money to make a colossal misfire
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: It's hard not to applaud Joy's ambition with Reminiscence. She's swinging for the fences and trying to incorporate several different stories, themes, and sci-fi elements. Joy just struggles to bring them all together in a cohesive fashion.
reviews.author: Charlie Ridgely

reviews.text: ...mixes the old and the new with high-flying flair...
reviews.author: Erin Free

reviews.text: Inventive and ambitious but wildly convoluted and ultimately disappointing.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: You have to really buy into some shared connections if you want to be motivated by where all of this is going.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: The film doesn't do much to distinguish itself, or to retain audience interest.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: But the film never fully capitalizes on the ideas of its sci-fi premise promises, nor does it marry its clear love of classic film noir to a visual style worthy of the lineage it pays lip service to.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: If you are into science fiction thrillers that make you think you have it all figured out before they rip the rug right out from underneath you, Reminiscence is for you.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: I'm not sure future slow-burn classic status awaits, but at a time when few studio films even seem to be striving for it, you have to applaud the attempt.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: there is just too much flotsam and jetsam in this waterlogged effort, drowning the film's better aspects. The sad irony of "Reminiscence" is that it will soon be forgotten.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: When Joy lets us peek in these tiny, intriguing corners of her speculative world, Reminiscence comes alive the most. Otherwise, the rest of it fades like a memory you'd just as soon forget.
reviews.author: Clint Worthington

reviews.text: Jackman is a charismatic performer, but always within a certain narrow bandwidth. Ferguson, for all the hype, has an even smaller range. Together they are screen poison.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: The ambitious but flawed Reminiscence spirals and coils around the beginnings and endings of stories, a veritable Möbius pretzel of meaty meta musings.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: A daring and futuristic sci-fi story based in a familiar genre and driven by familiar human emotions: love, loss, betrayal, regret.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: Reminiscence is clearly aiming for a classic, noir-style vibe with a sci-fi twist, but it misfires/miscalculates at almost every turn ... to conjure entirely the wrong atmosphere.
reviews.author: Mark Cassidy

reviews.text: An abysmal Strange Days clone
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: It's an ingenious, taut neo-noir with the right amount of romance and intrigue.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: For every scene that works - and there are plenty - there's one that goes off the rails.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: Intriguing but ultimately shallow...
reviews.author: G. Allen Johnson

reviews.text: With its unabashed old soul and classic appetite for what makes a great Hollywood tale, "Reminiscence," is all about gorgeous movie stars intertwined, mysteries that throw characters into emotional labyrinths.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: Excellent performances from Hugh Jackman, Thandiwe Newton, and Rebecca Ferguson, in addition to some gorgeous production design choices, make this an intriguing watch.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Its star cast notwithstanding, there's good reason Warners is dumping the movie in the dog days of summer with minimal fanfare.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: This film is bustling with nods to the noir genre throughout. It often feels as though Joy can't seem to decide whether she wants her film to be a pastiche or a serious genre piece.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: This engrossing and compelling sci-fi detective yarn will make you nostalgic for when merely being a pretty good, star-driven, adult-skewing sci-fi original was enough to be a hit.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: For all its lovely looks, flashes of inspiration and splendid cast, Reminiscence mostly serves to remind you of other films -Minority Report, Blade Runner - that did similar future-noir much, much better.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: Reminiscence has a destination in mind, but the journey to get there is full of missteps and missed opportunities.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: "Reminiscence" plays like a perfectly calibrated two-hour mirage of things we've seen before.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Reminiscence immerses us quickly by offering something fresh and original in a world full of remakes and reboots.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: It's hard not to see it in algorithmic terms, for its personality is at times nothing more than an equation, one that pales next to the far superior films and shows it wants to sit next to, a drama about memory that's far too easy to forget.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: It's an absolute slog to watch Jackman row this way and that in search of something to justify this movie's labored metaphors.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Reminiscence is so beholden to the tropes of the genre that it begins to feel like it's constantly winking at its audience.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

synopsis: Nick Bannister (Hugh Jackman), a private investigator of the mind, navigates the darkly alluring world of the past by helping his clients access lost memories. Living on the fringes of the sunken Miami coast, his life is forever changed when he takes on a new client, Mae (Rebecca Ferguson). A simple matter of lost and found becomes a dangerous obsession. As Bannister fights to find the truth about Mae's disappearance, he uncovers a violent conspiracy, and must ultimately answer the question: how far would you go to hold on to the ones you love?
